messages:
maria_nguyen: Heads-up — got a postmortem draft for short-notice GPU losses. proposing a 'soft offload' flow rather than immediate hard abort. idea: stream-token cutover + ephemeral standby buffer nodes.
ajay_shah: high level? how does soft offload differ from current drain+requeue?
samir_khan: current flow: eviction -> SIGTERM -> try graceful finish -> if timeout requeue. we lose in-flight streaming clients and their KV cache.
elaine_wu: +1 on preserving user-visible streaming continuity. customers hate a sudden stream reset.
maria_nguyen: exactly. soft offload = keep the existing connection streaming but proxy subsequent tokens from a standby node that has the session's KV stitched. steps: 1) graceful drain attempt on source 2) if eviction still incoming, snapshot minimal KV + prefetch last N tokens to S3/cache 3) warm standby applies snapshot and starts accepting new tokens 4) router switches token stream to standby with helper tokens.
ajay_shah: how long to snapshot? we need <5s for 90th perc.
samir_khan: depends on prefix length. propose delta snapshot: only changed KV pages plus last 512 tokens. we measured ~300-700ms for 512 tokens on NVLink local fs in lab. across network maybe 1.2s median to cached node in same region.
elaine_wu: what's the handshake protocol? any code sample?
maria_nguyen: draft handshake pseudo:```
POST /v1/_handshake {"session_id":"s123","evicting_node":"n1","standby":"n23","kv_pages":["p1","p2"],"last_tokens":"base64(...)"}
standby replies 200 + ready:true + resume_token:"rt_abc"
router swaps stream token: X-Resume-Token: rt_abc
```
ajay_shah: resume_token is ephemeral with short TTL. good. how do we avoid double-exec if both nodes accept?
samir_khan: allot soft-lock TTL during cutover: router marks session owned_by:standby once resume_token issued. source node stops emitting tokens after ACK. we also add monotonic seq numbers embedded in chunks to detect dupes.
elaine_wu: edge: what if no standby available in region? fallbacks?
maria_nguyen: fallback policy: a) same-region standby b) cross-region standby (if latency budget allows) c) graceful requeue to client with resume instructions d) last resort: truncated final chunk + reason code.
ops-oncall: ops question — cost implications? keeping standbys warm will cost $$ unless using tiny cheap GPUs or CPU-only proxies.
ajay_shah: suggestion: mixed-capacity pool: keep cheap ephemeral CPU-based samplers that can continue streaming but at degraded throughput. customers see slight latency bump instead of reset.
samir_khan: quantization-friendly checkpoint snapshots let small-instance runtime produce tokens for short tail. cost math: warm tiny nodes at 10% of fleet cost reduces failure rate by ~80% in our sim.
elaine_wu: metrics we should emit: cutover_latency, snapshot_size_bytes, resume_success_rate, duplicate_chunks_detected, cost_per_cutover. add tagging by customer_tier.
maria_nguyen: rollout plan: implement handshake + resume_token in canary region (us-west2) behind feature flag, run 2 weeks, compare SLOs and cost.
ops-oncall: add alert if resume_success_rate < 95% over 5m. also add a dashboard for 'soft-offload heatmap' by node pool.
infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary/soft-offload-handshake v0.1 -> staging at 2204123520 by ci/cd
ajay_shah: implementation note: need kernel-level pinned memory flush for KV pages to avoid corruption when snapshotting. file: infra/kv_snapshot/README.md has earlier notes.
samir_khan: also need router change: emit X-Resume-Token and honor optimistic switch; update token accounting to charge original node for tokens produced until ack.
maria_nguyen: I'll push a PR with design doc + sequence diagrams. tagging @elaine_wu for SLO acceptance criteria and @ops-oncall for alert thresholds.
elaine_wu: LGTM — list of acceptance checks: 1) <1% client-visible resets in canary, 2) median cutover latency < 1.5s, 3) no data loss on KV in 1000 random sessions.
ops-oncall: copying postmortem templates to the PR so we can capture incidents during canary.
maria_nguyen: thanks all — will share link when PR's ready.
